name: Network Traffic Hunt
author: Network Defense Team
prerequisites: NetFlow v9/IPFIX or full PCAP available for hunt window
DNS query logging enabled on resolvers
Zeek or Suricata deployed at network boundary
required_tools: RITA (Real Intelligence Threat Analytics) for beaconing

hunt_actions.title: Command and Control Detection
actions: Hunt beaconing with RITA: `rita show-beacons <dataset> --limit 25 --human-readable` — review connections with Score > 0.7 and connection count > 50. Alternatively in Zeek conn.log: `cat conn.log | zeek-cut id.orig_h id.resp_h duration | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn | head -20` for repeated long-duration sessions.

Identify long-duration low-bandwidth sessions: `index=zeek sourcetype=zeek_conn | stats sum(bytes) as total_bytes, count as sessions, avg(duration) as avg_dur by src_ip, dest_ip | where avg_dur > 3600 AND total_bytes < 1048576 | sort -avg_dur` — sessions over 1 hour transferring less than 1 MB are suspicious.

Detect queries to newly registered domains (NRD): Use threat intel feed enrichment in Splunk: `index=dns | lookup nrd_lookup domain OUTPUT age | where age < 30 | stats count by query, answer, src_ip | sort -count` — or submit domains to https://whoisds.com/newly-registered-domains for manual lookups.

Hunt DNS over HTTPS (DoH) to unauthorized resolvers: `index=zeek sourcetype=zeek_conn dest_port=443 | lookup authorized_doh_resolvers dest_ip OUTPUT authorized | where isnull(authorized) | stats count by src_ip, dest_ip | sort -count` — known DoH providers: 1.1.1.1, 8.8.8.8, 9.9.9.9, 208.67.222.222.

hunt_actions.title: Data Exfiltration via Network
actions: Detect large outbound transfers to single external host: `index=zeek sourcetype=zeek_conn direction=outbound | stats sum(bytes_out) as total_out by src_ip, dest_ip | where total_out > 1073741824 | sort -total_out` — flag any single-destination transfer over 1 GB; investigate the destination with WHOIS and reputation check.

Hunt DNS tunneling via oversized or high-entropy queries: In Zeek dns.log: `index=zeek sourcetype=zeek_dns | eval qlen=len(query) | where qlen > 50 | stats avg(qlen) as avg_len, count by src_ip, query | where count > 100 AND avg_len > 60` — also check for query types TXT, NULL, MX used for tunneling (iodine, dnscat2).

Identify ICMP tunneling via non-standard payloads: `tshark -r capture.pcap -Y 'icmp' -T fields -e ip.src -e ip.dst -e icmp.type -e data.len | awk '$4 > 64'` — standard ICMP echo is 32-64 bytes; larger payloads indicate potential tunneling (ptunnel, icmptunnel).

Detect FTP and uncommon protocol usage from internal hosts: `index=zeek sourcetype=zeek_conn dest_port IN (21, 69, 513, 514, 23, 119, 135, 137, 138, 139) | stats count by src_ip, dest_ip, dest_port | sort -count` — these protocols should appear in an approved baseline; any unlisted use requires investigation.

hunt_actions.title: Lateral Movement Indicators
actions: Hunt SMB-based lateral movement: Windows Security Events 4648 (explicit creds) and 4624 Type 3 (network logon). Splunk: `index=windows EventCode=4648 TargetServerName!=localhost | table _time, host, SubjectUserName, TargetUserName, TargetServerName` — focus on source workstations authenticating to other workstations (not domain controllers).

Identify internal scanning behavior: `index=zeek sourcetype=zeek_conn | stats dc(dest_ip) as unique_dests count as attempts by src_ip, _time span=1h | where unique_dests > 50 | sort -unique_dests` — any internal host connecting to 50+ unique IPs in one hour is likely scanning; correlate with open ports to identify scan type.

Detect remote execution via PsExec, WMI, or DCOM: Sysmon Event 1 for PsExec (`Image=*psexec*` or `ParentImage=*services.exe* AND Image=*cmd.exe*`). For WMI lateral movement: Sysmon Event 20/21 (WmiEventConsumer). Splunk: `index=windows EventCode IN (4104,4688,1) (CommandLine=*psexec* OR CommandLine=*wmic* OR CommandLine=*winrm*) | table _time, host, CommandLine, ParentImage`

questions: Is full packet capture (PCAP) available for the hunt period, or are only flow records (NetFlow/IPFIX) and metadata logs available? What is the capture point(s) in the network?
What is the retention period for network flow logs and PCAP, and does it cover the suspected compromise window for this engagement?
Are Zeek or Suricata signatures current (updated within the last 7 days), and are rulesets tuned to suppress known-good traffic baselines specific to this environment?
Does the organization have a documented network traffic baseline defining normal traffic patterns, volumes, and authorized external communications for key host groups?
Are outbound firewall egress rules enforced with an explicit deny-all default, or is outbound traffic permissive by default?
Is DNS query logging enabled on all internal resolvers, including split-horizon or forwarder configurations, and are logs forwarded to the SIEM?
Is there a documented allowlist of authorized external egress points (proxies, VPN exit nodes, SaaS endpoints) that can be used to filter known-good traffic during the hunt?
Is network segmentation enforced between IT and OT/ICS networks, and are cross-segment communication rules documented and access-controlled?
